idiom_name: hand-written emitter functions (libxslt only when the source is already XML)
implementation_notes: C has no markup or XML support in its standard library, so the classic Transformer collapses into plain emitter functions: one function per domain struct that walks its fields and writes escaped text to a FILE* or a growable buffer with fputs/snprintf, plus a single escape helper for &, <, > and the quote characters. When the domain is already serialized to XML, libxslt provides the declarative route - xsltParseStylesheetFile compiles the stylesheet, xsltApplyStylesheet runs it over the document and xsltSaveResultToFile/xsltSaveResultToString serialize the result. The hand-written form stays justified when there is no XML stage and no libxml2/libxslt dependency is acceptable.
pitfalls: No escaping by default: every text and attribute write must go through one escape helper, or user data breaks the markup and injects HTML.
Buffer discipline: snprintf truncation and off-by-one writes corrupt output silently; prefer a growable buffer with explicit length tracking over fixed char arrays.
libxslt keeps process-global state and its objects must be freed explicitly (xsltFreeStylesheet, xmlFreeDoc, xsltCleanupGlobals, xmlCleanupParser) or every request leaks.

variants.name: libxslt stylesheet pipeline
variants.implementation_notes: The declarative realization: the transformer is a stylesheet applied to an XML serialization of the domain. Parse the stylesheet once with xsltParseStylesheetFile, run xsltApplyStylesheet per request, serialize with xsltSaveResultToString or xsltSaveResultToFile, and free everything explicitly; parameters travel as a NULL-terminated name/value array. Choose it when the domain is already XML and the presentation must change without recompiling.
pitfalls: A compiled stylesheet holds mutable parameter state: do not share one xsltStylesheetPtr across threads while setting parameters.
libxslt does not safely process untrusted stylesheets - it can read the file system and the network - so stylesheets are trusted code.
